Chapter 3: Discovering the World Through Books and Curiosity.
With the worst days of the famine finally behind them, you could feel the village slowly coming back to life. The fields are being planted again, and there’s this gentle sense of hope—everyone’s quietly wishing for a better harvest this time. But for our boy, even though his stomach isn’t empty anymore, his hunger for knowledge just keeps growing. Going back to school isn’t possible yet, but he’s not about to let that stop him.
So, what does he do? He gets creative. He turns to the tiny local library—sure, it’s a bit dusty and the shelves are pretty bare, but to him, it’s a treasure trove. He dives into whatever he can find, from old textbooks to dog-eared magazines, soaking up every scrap of information about science, technology, and the world beyond his village. Sometimes the words are tough, and the ideas are even tougher, but he sticks with it—reading, rereading, and slowly making sense of things that once seemed impossible.
Then, one afternoon, he comes across a book that changes everything—a guide to energy and electricity. Suddenly, he’s staring at pictures of windmills and generators, and it sparks his imagination. He starts to wonder: what if the wind that sweeps over these plains every day could actually be turned into power? The idea is simple, but it feels revolutionary. If he could build a windmill, maybe he could light up his own home, or even help his village water their crops. Just imagine the difference it could make.
Of course, turning that dream into reality isn’t easy. He doesn’t have formal training, or fancy tools, or even the right parts. But what he does have is pure curiosity and a stubborn determination to figure things out. So he heads to the local scrapyard, hunting for treasure among the trash—old bike parts, scraps of wire, odd bits of metal. Every piece he finds brings him a little closer to his goal, and each discovery feels like a small victory.
Most folks in the village? They watch from a distance. Some laugh, some shake their heads, certain he’s wasting his time. Their doubt stings, but the boy just keeps going. He works quietly, testing and tinkering behind the scenes, and every time something doesn’t work, he learns a bit more. It’s slow, and sometimes it’s frustrating, but each setback just makes him more determined to succeed.
Little by little, he starts to understand how electricity works, how gears and levers fit together. The windmill begins to take shape, piece by piece—a testament to what’s possible when you’re driven by curiosity and the courage to keep asking, “What if?”
And that’s the real lesson here. Education isn’t just about sitting in a classroom. It’s about a lifelong quest for answers—a journey fueled by curiosity, imagination, and the guts to keep going, even when no one else believes you can.
